Rangers Respond to Character Debate Ahead of Semi-Final

Manager Derek McInnes has defended his Rangers squad against recent internal criticism regarding the team's character, following a 2-2 draw against Hearts on Wednesday.

Speaking ahead of the upcoming League Cup semi-final against Aberdeen, scheduled for Saturday, McInnes addressed post-match remarks made by defender Olwethu Makhanya.

Wednesday's Match and Internal Reaction

During Wednesday's fixture, Rangers secured a 2-2 draw thanks to an 89th-minute header by Makhanya. However, the defender stated after the match that there was a "lack of character" from the team at the start of the second half, adding that Hearts "showed more desire" and outworked Rangers to overturn the game.

Responding to those comments, McInnes stated that it is "too easy to point fingers at character," a term he argued "gets bandied about."

According to the manager, physical metrics indicated a strong work rate:

  • Running Stats: McInnes noted that physical data showed the team was not lacking in effort.
  • Late Resilience: The squad demonstrated determination by recovering a result in the closing stages.
  • Technical Shortfalls: McInnes acknowledged that the team fell short technically and physically during certain phases, noting they were second best, got outmuscled, and reacted slowly to loose balls.

Upcoming Fixture and Verification

Rangers are preparing to face Aberdeen in the League Cup semi-final on Saturday. McInnes emphasized that the squad is continuing to learn through experience as the season progresses.
